newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. court clears extradition of Sikh to India.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court clears extradition of Sikh to India.

text.p: A U.S. court has cleared the extradition to India of a suspected Sikh militant leader wanted by New Delhi for a bus bombing and an attempted political assassination, officials said on Tuesday.

Officials of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police agency, said a Texas court had cleared the way for the extradition of Daya Singh Sandhu, who was arrested in Minneapolis in 1995.

Sandhu, also known as Lahoria, was believed to be one of the leaders of the Khalistan Liberation Force, a militant outfit fighting for a separate Sikh nation in the northern state of Punjab bordering Pakistan.

Sandhu was wanted in India in several crimes, including a bus bombing that killed eight and injured 29. CBI officials said he was wanted in the attempted assassination in 1994 of the former head of the Congress party's youth wing, M.S. Bitta.
Sandhu was arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service in August 1995 at the Minneapolis-St Paul airport and charged with illegal entry into the United States and visa fraud.
India had sought the help of Interpol in gaining his extradition, CBI officials said.
